name: Rheon Systems SoftShell Ballistic Underlayer
description: Worn under civilian clothing, the SoftShell is a full-torso soft ballistic underlayer in off-white with Rheon's triple-hex pattern embossed subtly across the surface. The material is a non-Newtonian smart composite — pliable and light at rest, rigidifying on sudden impact across the strike zone. Slim enough to hide under a dress shirt or fitted jacket without obvious bulk. The neck and underarm panels are perforated for airflow. A faint chemical smell dissipates within an hour of first wear.
functionality: Rated for low-velocity ballistic and blade-edge impact across torso and upper back. Smart-stiffening activates on impact without requiring power. Chrome-port bypass channels route implant cabling cleanly through the torso without creating pressure points or ballistic weak spots.
what_it_says: You have enough enemies to warrant armor and enough taste to hide it.
story_hooks: A SoftShell was recovered from a crime scene with a strike deformation pattern that doesn't match any registered weapon caliber in the M88 database.
Rheon quietly recalled a batch of Mark IIIs for a stiffening failure — but the recall notice never reached the black market units already in circulation.
A corporate fixer was photographed at a peace summit — image analysis suggests they're wearing a SoftShell under diplomatic clothing, which is a treaty violation.
